questions.question: State the observation made when bromine water is added to a solution of 2‑butene and explain the chemical reason for this observation.
Describe the mechanism for the electrophilic addition of HBr to 1‑hexene, indicating the role of the double bond and the formation of the carbocation intermediate.
Explain why the reaction of 2‑pentene with HBr gives a major product and a minor product, and identify which product is formed in greater quantity.
Calculate the percentage of bromine that is consumed when 0.50 g of 1‑butene (MW = 58.12 g mol⁻¹) reacts with excess Br₂. (Molar mass of Br₂ = 159.8 g mol⁻¹)
Compare the reactivity of 1‑hexene and 2‑hexene towards HBr and justify your answer using the stability of the intermediate carbocation.
A polymerisation reaction of ethene is carried out using a Ziegler–Natta catalyst. State the repeating unit of the polymer formed and explain why this polymer is a linear chain.
Describe the test that can be used to confirm the presence of a carbon–carbon double bond in an unknown hydrocarbon and explain the chemical basis of the test.
Explain how the addition of H₂SO₄ to 1‑butene leads to the formation of a tertiary alcohol, detailing the steps of the mechanism.

A student records the following data: 0.30 g of 2‑hexene (MW = 84.16 g mol⁻¹) reacts with excess Br₂. The product is isolated as a single compound weighing 0.45 g. Calculate the yield of the addition product and state the likely product formed.
Evaluate the environmental impact of using bromine water as a test for unsaturation in industrial waste streams, considering both effectiveness and safety.
